Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module six on corrosion chemistry and today's class we are going to talk about yet another method of corrosion control and that is cathodic protection.

Key details

  • In that there are two ways, one is known as the sacrificial anon method, the other is known as impressed cathodic current method.
  • To be protected into cathode.
  • This is coming from the electrochemical theory of corrosion, where we understand that it's only the anode which undergoes corrosion, whereas the cathode remains unaffected.
  • The structure to be protected is completely converted into cathode and no part of it is allowed to act as anode.
  • And we know that since cathode does not undergo corrosion, so the structure is completely protected from corrosion.
  • One is known as the sacrificial annode method, and the other is the impressed current method.
  • Now in this method.
  • Remember that we have to convert the metal into cathode.
  • One good way would be if it is connected to a more active metal.
  • In contact with the cathodic metal, the cathodic metal gets protected completely as long as the anodic metal is present in contact with the cathodic metal, the it is the anode which undergoes corrosion.
  • Concept is used here.
  • They are zinc and magnesium.
  • most of the times and these are referred to as auxiliary anode.
  • Now why do we call it as the sacrificial anode method?
  • This is referred to as the sacrificial anode method for the simple reason that in order to protect the structure, metallic structure, we are sacrificing the metal which is acting as the anode.
  • Hence, this is known as the sacrificial anode method.
  • The only problem with this method is that as the anodes get exhausted, they have to be replaced periodically because we have to understand that the cathode structure now is protected only.
  • as long as it is in contact with an anode metal.
  • Magnesium and zinc bars which are fixed to sides of ocean going ships.
  • Ship is getting protected just by attaching a magnesium or zinc bar onto the surface, of course.
  • It is not that we put a small zinc bar and a whole big ship is protected.
  • Yes, it is done by calculation and at regular intervals these magnesium you can see here also so many of them are placed here.
  • Regular intervals these magnesium or zinc bars are pr are attached to the body of the ship and that is going to protect the big huge ship from corrosion.
  • very pipeline, we find that the pipeline is protected from corrosion.
  • Again, it has to be kept at regular intervals.
